title: Emrys and the Oath
premise: Kestrel Ishikawa makes his living in the Valley of Hollow, a place where magic cannot enter and the old gods have been silent for three hundred years — by stealing memories from travelers who cross its border and selling them back to those desperate to forget. When prayers begin reaching the old gods again through him, Kestrel discovers he is the last living vessel of the Oath, a covenant between gods and mortals that was shattered when his grandmother sealed the valley. Hunted by a god-king who wants the Oath reforged under his dominion, and haunted by stolen memories that may not all belong to strangers, Kestrel must journey beyond the valley into a world where every step costs him pieces of himself. In the end, he learns the broken covenant can only be remade by someone willing to give up their own memory entirely — and he pays that price, becoming the new oath-bearer: nameless, remembered by no one, but holding the realms together as the long winter breaks.
about_author: Mirabel Reyes is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing oral histories from mountain villages before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about memory, inheritance, and the small betrayals families keep, and lives somewhere with unreliable winters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. On market day in the Valley of Hollow, Kestrel lifts a soldier's memory of a burning city and sells it to a grieving widow who wants her own past erased instead. The transaction goes smoothly until the soldier's memory flickers with something impossible: a god's face. Beat: restless competence masking emptiness.

chapters.title: Prayers in a Godless Place
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. That night Kestrel dreams someone else's prayer — a child begging the river god for spring — and wakes with frost on his windows in a valley where magic cannot follow. His fence, Odile, warns him that things which answer prayers also collect debts. Beat: first crack in the safe world.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Remembered Him Wrong
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. A stranger arrives claiming to know Kestrel — calling him by a childhood name he's never heard — then dies at the valley border as if something tore the memory of him out of her mid-sentence. Among her effects: an oath-token bearing his family crest. Beat: dread; identity begins to wobble.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Locked Room
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Searching his dead grandmother's house, Kestrel finds a hidden chamber of stolen god-memories, each vial labeled in her hand, and one empty slot with his own name on it. The house itself seems to resist him. Beat: betrayal across generations; the valley's peace revealed as a cage.

chapters.title: What Crosses the Border
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. The god-king Veyran's herald arrives at the valley edge, unable to enter, and offers Kestrel passage, protection, and truth in exchange for coming out willingly. Kestrel refuses — then finds the valley's wards failing around his own body. Beat: cornered; the choice is no longer a choice.

chapters.title: Leaving Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Kestrel crosses the border with Odile as reluctant guide, and magic floods back into him like cold water — including memories that aren't his, surfacing unbidden. The world beyond is deep in an early, wrong winter. Beat: disorientation and awe; grief for the self he was inside.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Traveling through villages where minor gods still linger in shrines and wells, Kestrel learns the old gods are waking ragged and starving because the covenant that fed them broke three centuries ago. Some beg him for help; some try to eat his memories. Beat: wonder curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Odile reveals she once served Veyran and that she guided Kestrel out partly to redeem a debt — she helped his grandmother seal the valley and steal the god-memories. She believes returning them will end the winter. Beat: trust fractured and rebuilt on harder terms.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. They reach Ashfall, capital of the god-king's realm, where citizens wear memory-tokens and cannot recall their own histories without them — Veyran's model for all mortals. Kestrel recognizes the architecture of his grandmother's theft, scaled up. Beat: horror at power perfected.

chapters.title: Audience with the God-King
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Veyran receives Kestrel courteously, shows him the shattered covenant-stone, and offers partnership: reforge the Oath together, with Veyran holding the divine half and mortals keeping only what he permits. He hints he knew Kestrel's grandmother intimately. Beat: seductive temptation; the villain is almost reasonable.

chapters.title: Memories That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Fleeing the palace, Kestrel is ambushed by his own surfacing memories: a temple, a sister, a promise made before the valley existed. He realizes the 'empty vial' held his original life — his grandmother stole his identity to hide him. Beat: identity crisis peaks; grief and fury.

chapters.title: The Sister in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Following the memory-threads, Kestrel finds Sef, alive, now a wandering priestess of the dying river god — and older than she should be, sustained by the same stolen years. Their reunion is tender and accusatory in equal measure. Beat: love complicated by theft; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Winter's Teeth
chapters.summary: POV Odile. The long winter accelerates; a village they shelter in freezes from the inside as its god dies mid-prayer. Odile confesses the full ritual of reforging requires a mortal vessel to hold the Oath — and that vessel must surrender all personal memory. Beat: mounting dread; the cost comes into view.

chapters.title: Theft Turned Inside Out
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Kestrel attempts to return the stolen god-memories to their owners and discovers each act of restitution weakens him — he is the container they were hidden in, and giving them back is slowly erasing him. Sef begs him to stop. Beat: sacrifice begins; heroism has a physical toll.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Shrine
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Veyran's hunters, led by the resurrected stranger from chapter three, capture Sef and the recovered memories. Kestrel learns the stranger was his friend in the forgotten life — now hollowed into Veyran's tool. Beat: devastating loss; the enemy wears a beloved face.

chapters.title: The Empty Vial
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. Imprisoned in Ashfall, Kestrel confronts the last stolen memory: his grandmother's confession — she sealed the valley not to protect him but because she could not bear to watch him become what Veyran demanded. He forgives her, and chooses. Beat: acceptance; resolve forged from grief.

chapters.title: Storming the Covenant-Stone
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel and Odile alternating. With Sef freed by sympathetic minor gods, the trio assaults the palace sanctum during the solstice dark, when Veyran's power ebbs. Odile holds the door alone against the hollowed stranger. Beat: kinetic climax begins; loyalty tested in blood.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel. At the shattered stone, Kestrel pours the returned god-memories into the covenant and speaks the Oath — but Veyran seizes the moment to bind it to himself. Kestrel counters by offering the only currency left: his entire remembered self, name and all. Beat: climax; the ultimate price paid willingly.

chapters.title: Nameless
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The Oath takes hold; the winter breaks. But Kestrel stands blank-eyed among the ruins, knowing nothing, while Veyran — stripped of stolen divinity — flees diminished into the mountains. Sef holds her brother's hand and introduces herself to him as a stranger. Beat: bittersweet aftermath; victory with a wound at its center.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Sef. The restored gods offer the nameless man a place among them; instead he asks to learn the world again from the beginning. Sef begins telling him stories — starting with a thief in a valley, leaving out the ending. Beat: tenderness; memory reborn as gift rather than possession.

chapters.title: Spring in Hollow
chapters.summary: POV Kestrel (the nameless one). They travel back to the valley, whose wards dissolve now that the covenant lives again. He feels echoes in places he can't explain — a locked room, a market stall — and smiles without knowing why. Beat: quiet homecoming; identity as something grown, not given.

chapters.title: The New Oath-Bearer
chapters.summary: POV Sef, closing epilogue. A year later, prayers reach the old gods easily, and mortals carry their memories freely. The nameless man tends the covenant-stone, and when children ask his name he says, honestly, that he is still choosing it. Final image: green returning to the high passes. Beat: hopeful resolution; the theme answered — identity is not what you remember, but what you do next.
